papers.title: Proton generalized parton distributions from electromagnetic form factors: A theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction
papers.summary: We present a theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction of the unpolarized, chiral-even, leading-twist proton generalized parton distributions $H^q$ and $E^q$. At zero skewness, valence-quark distributions are combined with flavor-dependent exponential profiles calibrated simultaneously against phenomenological representations of the proton and neutron electromagnetic form factors. The construction imposes exact valence and anomalous-magnetic-moment normalizations, the low-scale condition $B^{u+d}(0)=0$, the required endpoint behavior, and the complete Gaussian impact-parameter positivity bound. The resulting parametrization provides a reasonable description of the electromagnetic form factors and their slopes while revealing the tension between strict GPD consistency and a precision reproduction of all low-$Q^2$ observables within the adopted ansatz. We extend the distributions to nonzero skewness using normalized double distributions and introduce an independent $D$-term to complete the relevant Mellin polynomials. We examine electromagnetic and energy--momentum-tensor form factors, impact-parameter distributions, positivity, polynomiality, and illustrative mechanical properties. The analysis distinguishes information constrained by electromagnetic data from additional assumptions governing skewness and the mechanical sector, thereby providing a transparent elastic baseline for future studies of nucleon-to-resonance transition GPDs.

papers.title: Indirect probes of heavy neutral leptons through the dipole portal at FCC-ee
papers.summary: We study indirect probes of the gauge-invariant dipole portal of Majorana heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) at FCC-ee. Virtual HNLs modify electroweak gauge-boson propagation and lepton couplings through loops with two dipole interactions. We calculate the resulting finite matching corrections and their effects on $Z$-pole observables. For real, flavour-aligned couplings, the local response is specified by four combinations of coupling shifts. Independent local ultraviolet interactions can reproduce all four, making the dipole interpretation dependent on assumptions about those interactions. With improved Standard Model predictions, FCC-ee can probe equal, same-sign hypercharge and weak dipole coefficients as small as $0.14\,\mathrm{TeV}^{-2}$ at an HNL mass of 1 TeV. This projection assumes dipole dominance, with independent ultraviolet coefficients set to zero at twice the HNL mass. We quantify how additional ultraviolet contributions can weaken or strengthen the sensitivity. At 1 TeV, the projected reach is competitive with HL-LHC same-sign dilepton searches for Majorana HNLs, while larger masses allow smaller dipole coefficients to be probed within the effective theory's domain of validity. Radiative Higgs decays offer a modest further improvement. The FeynRules, FeynArts and UFO models used in this analysis are publicly available at \href{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23667622}{doi:10.5281/zenodo.23667622}.

papers.title: Top Spin and CP from Equivariant Transformers
papers.summary: Measurements of spin correlations and CP are an exciting and challenging part of the precision-LHC program. We first show how L-GATr-slim, as a Lorentz-equivariant transformer, significantly boosts the spin analyzing power for hadronic top quarks. We then show how adding a pseudoscalar channel to its architecture allows us to learn and interpret optimal observables and their CP properties. We demonstrate this for WBF-Higgs production at parton level and top pair production including detector effects.

papers.title: The Search for the Top Quark
papers.summary: The discovery of the top quark in 1995 completed the roster of the matter particles, quarks and leptons, expected in the Standard Model and in many of its suggested extensions. However, the top quark does not conform to the pattern set by its sister quarks and has come to be a critical component of the ongoing searches for physics beyond the prevailing paradigm. (Prepared for the Proceedings of the 4th International Symposium on the History of Particle Physics, CERN, Nov. 2025.)
papers.comments: 15 pages, 4 figures, Proceedings of the 4th International Symposium on the History of Particle Physics, CERN, November 2025

papers.title: Photon-Counting Readout via Electro-Optic Microwave-to-Optical Transduction for Axion Haloscopes
papers.summary: Axion dark matter searches require highly sensitive detection schemes with high scan rate to efficiently explore the parameter space. Building upon the conventional Sikivie haloscope, where axions convert into microwave photons inside a magnetic-field-immersed resonant cavity, we present a photon-counting scheme based on an electro-optic microwave-to-optical transducer. Through a comprehensive theoretical model under realistic experimental constraints, we find that the optimal operating regime employs an overcoupled microwave cavity, trading peak transduction efficiency for reduced transducer noise. Furthermore, combining parameters already demonstrated in existing devices, in a device with optimized extrinsic coupling rates, would yield a scan-rate enhancement of 5-10 relative to quantum-limited homodyne detection. Improvements in quality factors, coupling rates, and thermal management push this enhancement beyond 50. While our quantitative model is benchmarked at 9 GHz, the scheme adapts well to haloscopes across the 5-12 GHz range, where shrinking cavity volumes severely degrade the achievable scan rate. These results demonstrate the potential of electro-optical photon detection as a high-speed detection technique for axion dark matter searches.

papers.title: Projected sensitivity of the \anubis detector to photophobic and fermion-coupled axion-like particles
authors: Paul Swallow for the ANUBIS Collaboration
papers.summary: Axion-like particles (ALPs) are a common benchmark for experiments at the lifetime frontier, as their suppressed couplings to Standard Model particles can render them long-lived on detector scales. This article presents the projected sensitivity of the ANUBIS detector at the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) to two scenarios: a photophobic ALP model and a modified version of the flavour-diagonal, fermion-coupled ALP benchmark of the Physics Beyond Colliders initiative that introduces an additional $h\to Za$ decay. For the photophobic case, the ANUBIS detector will reach a peak sensitivity of $σ_{Wa}\cdot Br(a\rightarrow gg)=6.2\times10^{-4}$~pb at $cτ=1.95$ m for an ALP mass of $10$ GeV. This will improve on the current exclusion limits from the ATLAS experiment by two orders of magnitude and extend the $cτ$ coverage by three orders of magnitude. For the fermion-coupled case with a dimension-seven Higgs--ALP interaction, the peak sensitivity to the fermion coupling is $C_{a^Φ}=4.4\times10^{-8}$, reached for ALP masses between $16$ and $23$ GeV. Overall, the ANUBIS detector is shown to provide unique coverage of the parameter space of both models, in regions that can be probed neither by the main LHC experiments nor by forward detectors at the HL-LHC.

papers.title: Pionization experiments in light nuclei
papers.summary: The zero-energy antiproton absorption in light nuclei is considered. The ratios $R_{n/p}$ of antiproton-neutron versus antiproton-proton capture rates in the lightest nuclei $^2$H, $^3$He and $^4$He are analyzed, both from the experimental results and from some selected theoretical models. These models are used as key input in determining the level shifts and widths of the lowest states. We establish the capture orbit in $^3$He to be states of angular momentum $L=2$. Several N-N optical potentials are used to compute the $R_{n/p}$ values for several heavy nuclei and the results are found to be consistent with the data. However, the old chamber experiments studying pionization in Helium, are not consistent with models. Only the Paris potential is likely to succeed provided baryonia states predicted by this model are better understood.
papers.comments: To appear in Phys Rev C

papers.title: Search for heavy neutral leptons in top quark decays with same-sign, same-flavor dilepton final states in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
papers.summary: A search for a Majorana-type heavy neutral lepton (HNL) produced in top quark decays is reported. The search is based on proton-proton collision data at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$, collected during 2016$-$2018 with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC. In the type-I seesaw model, a Majorana HNL can mediate lepton-number-violating top quark decays. The search targets top quark pair production events in which one top quark decays into a bottom quark and a W boson, which subsequently decays into a charged lepton (electron or muon) and an HNL. The Majorana HNL then decays into a W boson and a charged lepton with the same sign and flavor as the one produced with the HNL. The experimental signature features a same-sign, same-flavor lepton pair and jets. The HNL masses between 20 and 100 GeV are probed. The data agree with the standard model background prediction. Observed (expected) upper limits at 95% confidence level are set on the branching fraction of the top quark decay into an HNL, a charged lepton, and a bottom quark, varying between [1.1 (0.71)] $\times$10$^{-5}$ and [4.8 (3.0)] $\times$10$^{-5}$ in the dielectron channel, and between [3.7 (3.4)] $\times$10$^{-6}$ and [2.4 (1.3)] $\times$10$^{-5}$ in the dimuon channel.
papers.comments: Submitted to the Journal of High Energy Physics. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/B2G-24-023 (CMS Public Pages)

papers.title: Multimuon Events from Cosmic Rays with the ALICE Detector
papers.summary: ALICE experiment at the CERN's Large Hadron Collider, carried out a cosmic data-taking campaign in the period 2015-2018 (LHC Run 2), for a total of 62.5 days of real observation time. In this contribution, the analysis of these data is limited to multimuon events, i.e. events with more than four detected muons. In particular, the muon multiplicity distribution (MMD) is studied in the low-intermediate multiplicity range ($4 < N_μ < 50$), while for multiplicities $N_μ > 100$, dominated by large statistical fluctuations of the data, the rate of the high muon multiplicity events (HMM) is measured. The results are compared with Monte Carlo simulations using three of the main hadronic interaction models describing the air shower development in the atmosphere: QGSJET-II-04, EPOS-LHC, and SIBYLL 2.3d, and assuming two extreme compositions of primary cosmic rays, pure proton and pure iron, representing respectively the lightest and the heaviest composition. Although the models have difficulty precisely describing the trend of primary p and Fe as a function of cosmic ray primary energy, QGSJET-II-04 is the only model that reproduces reasonably well the MMD and the rate of HMM events assuming a heavy composition for the entire energy range studied.

papers.title: A New Precise Measurement of the $e^+e^-\toπ^+π^-(γ)$ Cross Section with the Initial-State Radiation Method at BaBar
papers.summary: We report precise results for the $e^+e^-\to π^+π^-(γ)$ cross section in the energy range between threshold and 1.4 GeV, relevant for the hadronic vacuum polarization contribution to the muon $g-2$ prediction. Using the full 460 fb$^{-1}$ of on- and off-$Υ(4S)$ data, the cross section is derived from the ratio of $π^+π^-$ to $μ^+μ^-$ initial-state radiation (ISR) events, in which many systematic uncertainties cancel. The pion/muon separation does not rely on particle identification as in the 2009 BaBar analysis, but rather makes use of the well-known, different angular distributions in the two-particle center-of-mass system. The compatibility and correlation between the 2026 and 2009 measurements are discussed. The new measurement is also compared with other two-pion results. The leading-order hadronic contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly calculated using the new 2026 and combined 2009 and 2026 BaBar measurements in the energy range of 0.3$-$1.4 GeV are $525.9\pm 3.5_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.8_\mathrm{syst}$ and $517.8\pm 2.4_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.3_\mathrm{syst}$ in units of $10^{-10}$, respectively.

papers.title: A New Precise Measurement of the $e^+e^-\toπ^+π^-(γ)$ Cross Section with the Initial-State Radiation Method at BaBar
papers.summary: We measure the $e^+e^-\toπ^+π^-(γ)$ cross section from threshold to 1.4 GeV using 460 fb$^{-1}$ of BaBar initial-state radiation data. The result is obtained from the $π^+π^-/μ^+μ^-$ ratio, reducing systematic uncertainties that are in common. Unlike the previous 2009 BaBar analysis, the pion and muon contributions are separated statistically through their angular distributions. The compatibility with the previous BaBar result is quantified including statistical and systematic correlations. The new measurement is also compared with other two-pion results as a function of energy and in terms of its hadronic vacuum polarization (HVP) contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly. The leading-order HVP contribution of the two-pion channel in the energy range of 0.3$-$1.4 GeV is $a_μ^{ππ}=525.9\pm 3.5_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.8_\mathrm{syst}$ and $517.8\pm 2.4_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.3_\mathrm{syst}$ in units of $10^{-10}$ for the new 2026 and combined 2009 and 2026 BaBar measurements, respectively.

papers.title: A New Bound on Light-by-Light Scattering in the Low-Energy Regime
papers.summary: The superposition principle at the heart of optics states that electromagnetic fields do not interact in vacuum. This principle is not universal, instead electromagnetic fields couple weakly via quantum vacuum fluctuations. Striking consequences are light-by-light scattering and vacuum birefringence. Experimental results from colliding X-ray free-electron and optical high-intensity lasers combined with dark-field detection and polarimetry for background suppression are reported. This approach yields the most stringent bound for light-by-light scattering in the low-energy regime achieved to date -- improving upon previous experimental limits by ten orders of magnitude -- and paves the way for precision measurements.

papers.title: Modeling fragmentation of $^{20}$Ne nuclei at the LHC
papers.summary: Fragmentation of relativistic neon nuclei was studied with the Abrasion-Ablation Monte Carlo for Colliders model (AAMCC-MST), which incorporates pre-equilibrium clustering of spectator matter via a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) algorithm, subsequent decays of the excited clusters, and Coulomb repulsion between final fragments. After validating the model against data on $^{20}$Ne and $^{22}$Ne fragmentation on various targets, the production of spectator nuclear fragments, neutrons, and protons in $^{20}$Ne-$^{20}$Ne collisions at the LHC was modeled at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.36$ TeV. The production cross sections, transverse and longitudinal momentum distributions for $^2$H, $^4$He, $^6$Li, $^{10}$B, $^{12}$C, $^{14}$N, and $^{16}$O fragments were calculated as these fragments may contaminate $^{20}$Ne beams circulating in the LHC. A simple parametrization describing relative width of the longitudinal momentum distributions calculated for these fragment species was constructed. To study the sensitivity of results to $α$-clustering and nuclear density distributions in neon nuclei, two density profiles for $^{20}$Ne and $^{22}$Ne were used: a deformed Woods-Saxon, and a five-$α$ bi-pyramidal configuration. In addition, a spherical profile was considered for $^{20}$Ne. Comparing results obtained with these profiles and with or without MST clustering shows that the calculated yields of spectator nucleons and fragments, their momentum distributions are sensitive to the details of nuclear structure of $^{20,22}$Ne and fragmentation modeling. The results provide the input for simulations of the transport of secondary forward nuclei in the LHC to estimate their interaction rates with circulating $^{20}$Ne beam nuclei, and also for calculations of responses of neutron and proton Zero Degree Calorimeters to $^{20}$Ne-$^{20}$Ne events.

papers.title: The Cosmology of Hawking Axions
papers.summary: Since primordial black holes (PBH) are always non-relativistic, their cosmological energy fraction grows relative to that of radiation. Thus, for even a tiny initial PBH abundance, the universe generically enters an epoch of early matter domination, which ends when the PBH evaporate to restore the hot big bang. We consider the possibility that a PBH dominated era yields a population of boosted axion-like particles (ALPs) produced from Hawking evaporation. Eventually these ``Hawking axions" become non-relativistic and decay to photons, which can affect various cosmological and astrophysical observables. Here we place new constraints on these particles through their impact on big bang nucleosynthesis, cosmic microwave background, large-scale structure, and X-ray observables. Furthermore, if Hawking axions remain relativistic through recombination, then depending on the progenitor PBH mass, they contribute $ΔN_{\rm eff}\simeq0.05$-$0.11$, which may be observable with future CMB probes.

papers.title: Probing CP Violation in the Complex 2HDMS with a 95 GeV Scalar at Future $e^+e^-$ Colliders
papers.summary: In this study, we investigate the prospects for probing CP violation in the complex singlet extension of the two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM) at future electron-positron colliders. In extended scalar sectors, cancellations among different contributions to electric dipole moments (EDMs) can relax the stringent constraints on CP-violating phases, potentially bringing them in the current reach of collider experiments. We consider a scenario in which both the 125 GeV Higgs boson and the additional scalar associated with the reported 95 GeV excess are CP-mixed states. We probe the CP-violating phase of the 95 GeV scalar through its production via Higgsstrahlung and subsequent decay into a tau-lepton pair, using a CP-sensitive forward-backward asymmetry in hadronic and semileptonic tau-decay channels. We estimate the sensitivity at future lepton colliders, namely the ILC, FCC-ee, and CEPC, and investigate the impact of the Standard Model Drell-Yan background. We find that the hadronic channel offers greater sensitivity than the semileptonic channel. We also compare our results with existing constraints and future projections for CP violation in the 125 GeV Higgs sector and briefly discuss the implications for electroweak baryogenesis. Our results highlight the potential of future lepton colliders to probe CP violation in extended scalar sectors while remaining consistent with current EDM constraints.

papers.title: Gravitational waves flooding the Universe after wall domination
papers.summary: We discuss a possible early Universe scenario, where radiation era is interrupted by the epoch of domination of domain walls eventually annihilating into particles. During this period the Universe undergoes accelerated expansion, while the comoving correlation length of the domain wall network remains constant. The network serves as a source of tensor modes, which get frozen upon exiting the horizon similarly to the case of inflationary fluctuations. The modes re-enter the horizon during the subsequent stage of radiation domination and since then contribute to the gravitational wave background. The spectral shape of gravitational waves predicted in this scenario is markedly different compared to the case of domain walls remaining sub-dominant all the way till annihilation. These gravitational waves are strong enough to be observed with present-day and future facilities in a broad range of frequencies. In particular, their energy density is sufficient to produce a significant impact on the effective number of neutrino species, unless the duration of wall domination is suitably constrained.

papers.title: SMEFT Constraints on Top Electroweak Couplings and a Composite Higgs Interpretation
papers.summary: Recent LHC measurements of $tWZ$, $t\bar t Z$ and single top production provide complementary probes of top quark electroweak interactions. We incorporate these measurements into a global Standard Model effective field theory analysis of 46 independent dimension-six Wilson coefficients at linear order. The updated fit remains compatible with the Standard Model at $95\%$ CL, and favors negative values of $C_{Hq}^{(-)}\equiv C_{Hq}^{(1)}-C_{Hq}^{(3)}$ and $C_{Ht}$, with central values suggestive of TeV scale new physics. We also present an effective composite Higgs model based on a two-site description that realizes this pattern of Wilson coefficients through partial compositeness. The model includes custodial symmetry and protection of the $Z\bar b_L b_L$ coupling. A fermion bitriplet generates the required left-handed shift, and an additional embedding of the right-handed top allows negative contributions to $C_{Ht}$ from both fermion and spin-one exchange. Scanning four right-handed top embeddings, we find parameter regions within the $68\%$ CL contour that are compatible with electroweak precision data, Higgs coupling measurements and applicable direct searches. The $T$ parameter limits the negative fermionic contribution to $C_{Ht}$, favoring a spin-one contribution of comparable or greater magnitude. Larger $SU(2)_R$ representations extend the reach toward negative $C_{Ht}$, and also enhance four-quark interactions that increase the four-top cross section, in the direction favored by current measurements. The mechanism connects the preferred top electroweak shifts to complementary tests through single production of quarks with electric charge $-4/3$, modified Higgs couplings and four-top production.

papers.title: Goldstone theory of gluon saturation in high energy QCD: From color glass to color superfluid condensate
papers.summary: In the high energy Regge asymptotics of QCD, the rapid overpopulation of gluons leads to gluon saturation, characterized by nonperturbative semi-classical lumpy configurations of size $1/Q_S$, where $Q_S\gg Λ_{\rm QCD}$ is a dynamical semi-hard saturation scale. We discuss here a generalization of the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) framework describing this phenomenon that is obtained by carefully treating the breaking of global symmetries by the condensate. In particular, we show that the breaking of a global subgroup of color results in a Goldstone effective field theory (EFT) whose dynamics is characterized by a Goldstone decay constant $f_G = \sqrt{N} Q_S$, where $N=O(1/α_S)$ is the phase space occupancy of the condensate, which is large for $α_S(Q_S)\ll 1$. Further, the coupling of these colored Goldstones to collinear gluon modes leads to a depletion of the condensate, thereby modifying the static shockwave scattering framework of the CGC on timescales controlled by $f_G$. The CGC EFT on these longer time scales is a novel color superfluid. Low frequency modes with $ω\leq α_S Q_S$ in an external probe of the CGC are sensitive to superfluid dynamics, with interesting physical consequences for deeply inelastic scattering and ultrarelativistic nuclear collisions.

papers.title: Quantum computing for high energy nuclear physics
papers.summary: Quantum information science (QIS) offers a new set of conceptual and computational tools ideally suited to exploring the many-body, out-of-equilibrium, and real-time properties of strongly interacting quantum systems. These themes find a natural counterpart in high energy nuclear physics, whose central goal is to describe the properties of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), the theory of the strong interaction, under extreme conditions. Relevant examples range from the formation and internal structure of hadrons, to the collective and thermalization dynamics of strongly interacting QCD matter, and the properties of complex many-body scattering processes. Although tremendous progress has been made over the past decades in our understanding of QCD in the nuclear physics context, through perturbative methods, lattice QCD, and effective theory descriptions, phenomena that are intrinsically connected to real-time dynamics, highly entangled many-body evolution, or finite density regimes remain only partially accessible with existing approaches. In this article, we argue that QIS can help realize a new paradigm for addressing these open questions. With the aim of making the discussion accessible to both high energy nuclear physics and QIS audiences, we provide an overview of selected open problems in high energy nuclear physics, with emphasis on aspects motivated by collider phenomenology, and discuss how they can be approached using QIS tools. This connection is illustrated through representative examples drawn from the recent literature, making the case that QIS can become a driving force for discovery in nuclear physics in the coming years.

papers.title: Satisfying Freed--Witten quantization on smooth divisors in Calabi--Yau orientifolds
papers.summary: Freed--Witten quantization conditions on several divisors wrapped by D-branes must be satisfied with one bulk $B$-field. On a smooth Calabi--Yau threefold $X$ with a holomorphic O3/O7 involution $σ$, we show that the common background $B_{2,+}^{\star}=\tfrac12[R]$, where $R$ is the total O7 divisor, permits Freed--Witten period quantization on the full two-cycle lattice of \emph{every smooth connected divisor}, modulo torsion. The worldvolume fluxes are chosen individually and obey the orientifold relation between each divisor and its image. The central step concerns setwise invariant divisors $D$: we prove that the bulk Freed--Witten class $η_D^\star=\tfrac12([R]+[D])|_D$ has integer periods on every $σ$-even integral two-cycle class, including inherited and autochthonous classes. Its periods on purely $σ$-odd classes vanish, so any remaining non-integer periods occur only on classes that are neither $σ$-even nor $σ$-odd. We show how to choose $σ$-odd worldvolume fluxes on these invariant divisors that make all periods integral. For exchanged divisor pairs, quantizing the flux on one member automatically quantizes its orientifold image. On invariant divisors with $h^{2,0}_-(D)=0$, the constructed flux is of type $(1,1)$ and admits a primitive representative; this includes every smooth rigid invariant divisor. We also study zero worldvolume flux on invariant divisors. For $h^{1,1}_-(X)\leq1$, we construct common bulk backgrounds satisfying every inherited intersection period on all such divisors. A binary compatibility test determines whether a common shift exists for larger $h^{1,1}_-(X)$. Non-inherited period tests then determine whether the resulting backgrounds allow zero flux on the full worldvolume lattices.
papers.comments: 8+4 pages of main text and appendices

papers.title: Complete set of bounded-from-below conditions for the $A_4$-symmetric three-Higgs-doublet model
papers.summary: We derive bounded-from-below necessary conditions for the scalar potential of an $A_4$-invariant three-Higgs-doublet model. The field Ansätze that we have used were devised with the help of Claude. Testing our set of conditions on $10^6$ random potentials, that in parallel we minimize by brute force using the Mathematica package StableWein, we find that the set seems to be necessary and sufficient for boundedness-from-below.

papers.title: Dynamics of self-gravitating halos with decaying dark matter
papers.summary: We study the evolution of self-gravitating spherical dark matter halos composed of dark matter particles that decay to a slightly less massive particle and a massless particle. The small kick velocity imparted to the daughter particle upon decay heats the halo. If the kick velocity is small compared with the characteristic velocity, the halo remains bound but puffs out. We also consider, for the first time, decaying halos with anisotropic initial conditions and find non-negligible effects on the resulting density profile. To simulate the halo evolution, we utilize the recently developed \texttt{NSphere} code across a broad range of decay times and kick velocities. We train an emulator to provide a mapping between the decay parameters and the relaxed density profile. We discuss how the resulting halo-scale signatures complement existing cosmological constraints on decaying dark matter and can be tested by upcoming surveys.

papers.title: Flavour Chains at the TeV Edge
papers.summary: We study chains of vector-like fermions that generate the Yukawa hierarchies as products of small mixings, with the Higgs coupled at a single link. Minimal Flavour Protection allows these flavour messengers to live at the TeV scale, while Higgs naturalness offers a reason to place them there: in cosmological solutions based on Higgs criticality, their large multiplicity lowers the critical point of the Higgs potential to the TeV scale. Crucially, the same Higgs interactions induce tree-level shifts in the $Z$ and $W$ couplings of light fermions. Existing LEP and SLD measurements already bound $M_F/|y_F|\gtrsim 3$ TeV, while a future Tera-$Z$ factory such as FCC-ee could probe up to $100$ TeV. It would test the parameter space most relevant to Higgs naturalness, reaching scenarios with Higgs-mass tuning at the level of $10^{-4}$ or worse in minimal realisations. Longer chains partially alleviate this tuning but do not eliminate it, making a Tera-$Z$ factory a decisive test of the framework.

papers.title: Superconducting Qubits as Quantum Targets for Direct Particle Scattering
papers.summary: We introduce a novel approach to particle detection in which a superconducting qubit itself serves as the scattering target and a resolved transition between circuit eigenstates constitutes the observable final state. The scattering amplitude factorizes into the incident-particle current and a finite-momentum electromagnetic transition response of the qubit. This momentum dependence is essential in that the energy transfer is fixed by the microwave-scale level spacing, whereas a nonrelativistic incident particle can transfer a spatial momentum parametrically larger than that energy and thereby resolve the device geometry. For charge-dominated processes, we recast the response as an induced-offset-charge kernel obtained from an auxiliary electrostatic weighting potential, providing a practical route from circuit geometry to a differential scattering cross section. We illustrate the framework with an Xmon-style transmon and photon-mediated scattering of dark matter. The exceptionally small qubit transition threshold opens sensitivity to an eV-to-keV mass regime that is largely unexplored by existing direct-detection experiments.

papers.title: Probing Heavier-Baryon Oscillations through Light-Baryon Mixing
papers.summary: Motivated by the existing direct limits on $Ξ_b^0$ and $Ξ_c^0$ oscillations, we investigate how Standard Model weak interactions connect baryon-number-violating mixing in heavy neutral baryons to the much more strongly constrained neutron-antineutron and $Λ-\barΛ$ mixing. We focus on $Ξ_b^0$, $Λ_b^0$, $Ξ_c^0$, and $Ω_c^0$ oscillations and derive indirect constraints on their mass-mixing parameters from existing limits on $n-\bar n$ oscillations and on $Λ-\barΛ$ mixing, the latter inferred from dinucleon-decay searches. The weak baryon-to-baryon transition amplitudes are estimated by saturating the relevant hadronic correlators with low-lying intermediate baryons. The required weak vertices are modelled using semileptonic form factors from lattice QCD, quark models, and QCD sum rules. Since these form factors must be continued outside their physical semileptonic domains and the resulting loop integrals depend on a UV cutoff, our results are order-of-magnitude estimates subject to sizeable hadronic uncertainties. For a benchmark cutoff of $10~{\rm GeV}$, the indirect bounds on the $Ξ_b^0$ and $Ξ_c^0$ mixing parameters are roughly three and five orders of magnitude stronger than the direct LHCb and Belle limits, indicating that light-baryon $|ΔB|=2$ searches can probe heavy-baryon oscillations far beyond present direct sensitivities.

papers.title: Deconfinement Confined to the Heaviest Neutron Stars: Strange Quark Matter from a Flavor-Dressed Contact Interaction
papers.summary: We study cold, electrically neutral, beta-equilibrated quark matter with u, d, and s quarks described by a symmetry-preserving contact interaction whose parameters are fixed in vacuum. The vector repulsion is varied as a fraction 0 < eta < 3/2 of the scalar coupling, and results are given with and without the flavor dressing of the effective coupling. Pure quark matter is not self-bound in this model, and no value of eta produces a star that reaches two solar masses while satisfying the tidal constraint from GW170817; the heaviest configurations owe their mass to an envelope of constituent quarks. We then construct hybrid stars with a relativistic mean-field hadronic phase fitted to GM1 saturation properties, using both Maxwell and Gibbs constructions and a deconfinement bag shift. Tying deconfinement to chiral restoration and requiring a continuous pressure yields an upper bound on this shift. Within that bound, quark matter appears inside stable stars only for eta < 1/2, never below about 4 n0, and only in stars between 2.2 and 2.35Msun, over a stable mass window of at most 0.02Msun. The vector strength that pure quark stars need to become massive prevents deconfinement in hybrid stars. Radii and tidal deformabilities of intermediate-mass stars are therefore set by the hadronic EoS alone; with the softer SLy4 EoS the transition moves to the maximum-mass configuration itself.

papers.title: The Search for the Top Quark
papers.summary: The discovery of the top quark in 1995 completed the roster of the matter particles, quarks and leptons, expected in the Standard Model and in many of its suggested extensions. However, the top quark does not conform to the pattern set by its sister quarks and has come to be a critical component of the ongoing searches for physics beyond the prevailing paradigm. (Prepared for the Proceedings of the 4th International Symposium on the History of Particle Physics, CERN, Nov. 2025.)
papers.comments: 15 pages, 4 figures, Proceedings of the 4th International Symposium on the History of Particle Physics, CERN, November 2025

papers.title: Elliptic and triangular flow responses in O+O and Ne+Ne collisions from hydrodynamics and kinetic theory
papers.summary: Recent light-ion collisions at the Large Hadron Collider provide an opportunity to investigate the system-size dependence of hydrodynamization and whether the structure of light nuclei can be extracted from collective flow data. Both objectives require an accurate understanding of how the collision dynamics converts initial-state geometry into final-state momentum anisotropies. To this end, and to assess the impact of the experimental results, we compare simulations of O+O and Ne+Ne collisions in hydrodynamic and kinetic theory simulations across opacities. In both ultracentral and peripheral collisions, Ne+Ne-to-O+O elliptic flow ratios are robust against changes in dynamical description, supporting interpretations of data based on nuclear-geometry-driven effects. Triangular-flow ratios instead show substantially stronger sensitivity to nonequilibrium dynamics.

papers.title: Constraining tau-sterile neutrino mixing with high-energy astrophysical neutrinos
papers.summary: Whether a sterile neutrino mixes with the three active ones remains an open question. Its mixing with the tau neutrino, $|U_{τ4}|^2$, is the least constrained, since terrestrial experiments probe it only indirectly and over limited ranges of sterile-neutrino mass. We show that TeV-PeV astrophysical neutrinos probe it differently. Their sources make almost no $ν_τ$, but oscillations over cosmological distances turn about one third of them into $ν_τ$ before they reach Earth. Mixing with a sterile neutrino would make these $ν_τ$ scarcer, lowering the $ν_τ$ fraction that neutrino telescopes measure, whatever the sterile-neutrino mass. In contrast, sterile mixing with $ν_e$ or $ν_μ$ is nearly undetectable. Fitting the flavor composition measured by IceCube, with the composition at the sources left free, we find $|U_{τ4}|^2 < 0.88$ at 90% C.L. Combining IceCube with present and planned neutrino telescopes, including IceCube-Gen2 and HUNT, could lower this limit to 0.24-0.29 by 2040 and to 0.12-0.14 by 2050. By 2050, these limits would match some present terrestrial limits, though not the strongest.

papers.title: Photon-Counting Readout via Electro-Optic Microwave-to-Optical Transduction for Axion Haloscopes
papers.summary: Axion dark matter searches require highly sensitive detection schemes with high scan rate to efficiently explore the parameter space. Building upon the conventional Sikivie haloscope, where axions convert into microwave photons inside a magnetic-field-immersed resonant cavity, we present a photon-counting scheme based on an electro-optic microwave-to-optical transducer. Through a comprehensive theoretical model under realistic experimental constraints, we find that the optimal operating regime employs an overcoupled microwave cavity, trading peak transduction efficiency for reduced transducer noise. Furthermore, combining parameters already demonstrated in existing devices, in a device with optimized extrinsic coupling rates, would yield a scan-rate enhancement of 5-10 relative to quantum-limited homodyne detection. Improvements in quality factors, coupling rates, and thermal management push this enhancement beyond 50. While our quantitative model is benchmarked at 9 GHz, the scheme adapts well to haloscopes across the 5-12 GHz range, where shrinking cavity volumes severely degrade the achievable scan rate. These results demonstrate the potential of electro-optical photon detection as a high-speed detection technique for axion dark matter searches.

papers.title: Chiral anomalies in two dimensions
papers.summary: Chiral anomalies offer a fundamental probe of the quantum structure of gauge theories and their underlying symmetries. In this paper, we introduce a framework to characterize the chiral anomaly in two dimensions directly at the diagrammatic level. To this end, we establish a consistent prescription for handling $γ^5$ in dimensional regularization at $d=2$. On this basis, we derive an expression for the fully generic chiral anomaly directly from the contributions of the bubble and triangle diagrams, either in the massless or massive case. Then, we show that the different forms of the anomaly can arise from appropriate choices of parameters directly at the level of this master expression. Overall, $d=2$ is shown to provide an excellent environment to investigate chiral anomalies at the amplitude level: Ward identities are demonstrated rigorously and to arbitrary order in the mass expansion without further approximation, resulting in an unprecedented degree of control on the anomaly.

papers.title: Meson spectra in a screened relativized quark model
papers.summary: In this work, we employed the modified Godfrey--Isgur model to systematically investigate the mass spectra of several light, heavy-light, and heavy-heavy meson systems. In this model, a screened potential is employed to phenomenologically account for modifications to the long-range confining interaction associated with unquenched effects. We performed a global refit of the relevant model parameters to a combined set of 90 adopted meson masses spanning all three sectors, ensuring a consistent parameter determination across the different meson systems. Using the resulting parameter set, we calculated the low-lying and highly excited spectra and the corresponding mixed states in different meson families, and compared our results with existing experimental data and other theoretical results. The assignment of several newly observed structures (such as $B_c^*$ and $D_{s1}(2933)$) have also been discussed based on their predicted masses. Overall, the model describes several main spectroscopic features across different flavors and provides mass predictions for highly excited states that have not yet been experimentally established.

papers.title: Renormalization and Factorization Scale-Invariant Predictions for the $e^+e^-\to J/ψ+η_c$ process at $B$ factories
papers.summary: We perform a NNLO perturbative QCD analysis for exclusive double charmonium production $e^+e^-\to J/ψ+η_c$ within the NRQCD factorization formalism using the Principle of Maximum Conformality (PMC). It is well known that this charmonium process suffers poor pQCD convergence, as well as large renormalization scale uncertainty. The PMC is used to remove conventional renormalization scale uncertainty. Based on two fundamental physical processes of charmonium, $J/ψ\rightarrow e^+e^-$ and $η_c\rightarrowγγ$, and using the NNLO perturbative results together with experimental measurements, we extract the factorization-scale-dependent long-distance matrix elements for $J/ψ$ and $η_c$. Combining these two matrix elements with the factorization-scale-dependent short-distance coefficient, we obtain predictions that are independent of the factorization scale for the $e^+e^-\to J/ψ+η_c$ process. Our predictions agree with the measurement from the BaBar collaborations within errors. Remarkably, we provide a new way to eliminate conventional renormalization and factorization scale ambiguities for the $e^+e^-\to J/ψ+η_c$ process. We further demonstrate that the slow convergence of the pQCD series is an intrinsic property of this double-charmonium process.

papers.title: Probing the Spatial Coherence of Chiral-Imbalance Fluctuations with Hyperon Spin Correlations
papers.summary: Topological fluctuations in the quark-gluon plasma can generate local chiral imbalances whose spatial coherence remains difficult to access with conventional charge-separation measurements. We propose differential hyperon-pair spin correlations as a probe of both the strength and spatial organization of these fluctuations. Fluctuations of the axial chemical potential $μ_5$ can induce pair correlations even when the mean helicity polarization vanishes. Using the AMPT model, we find that the magnitude of the hyperon spin correlation probes the magnitude and spatial coherence scale of $μ_5$, while the ratio of short- and long-range correlations varies strongly with the spatial coherence scale, but only weakly with $μ_{5}$ over the range of explored parameters. These observables provide an experimentally testable strategy for constraining the spatial structure of chiral-imbalance fluctuations.

papers.title: On Photon Propagation in Strong Magnetic Fields: Time Delays from Pulsars
papers.summary: We study photon dispersion in the presence of a strong external magnetic field for propagation both perpendicular and parallel to the field, considering (i) the magnetized QED vacuum and (ii) a magnetized electron-positron medium at finite density (nonzero chemical potential). The analysis is performed in one-loop QED at finite temperature and density, and we extract polarization-dependent dispersion relations and phase velocities from the eigenmodes of the photon polarization operator. Using these phase velocities, we estimate propagation-induced time delays for photons emitted from neutron stars in the strong-field regime, adopting a simplified magnetosphere model with a toroidal magnetic field geometry and a radially varying chemical potential profile in the degenerate limit. We compare the predicted delays with observational timing constraints and discuss how strong-field QED and plasma corrections can generate measurable departures from the light cone, with potential signatures relevant for magnetars and modern polarimetric and timing observations. It should be noted that the time-delay estimates derived here are based on the phase velocity and serve as indicative order-of-magnitude predictions.

papers.title: Unitary $KK$ and $Kπ$ inputs for an amplitude analysis of the $D^+ \to K^-K^+π^+$ decay
papers.summary: Charge-Parity Violation (CPV) is expected in three-body charm decays. In particular, in the singly Cabibbo suppressed decay process $D^+ \to K^-K^+π^+$; in which an amplitude analysis is required to understand the dynamics of Final State Interactions (FSI) and the mechanism that can generate CPV. In this work, we show the prospects of analysing recent data from the Large Hadron Collider beauty (LHCb) experiment at CERN, with a precise theoretical model expected to reveal CPV mechanisms. Previous analyses of the $D^+ \to K^-K^+π^+$ decay were unable to satisfactorily describe the data using the Isobar Model. Currently, LHCb has a sample of charmed meson decays with around 100 million events for the $D^+ \to K^-K^+π^+$ decay, so a more robust phenomenological model is needed to describe such a large data set. The present model has allowed the inclusion of hadronic FSI and will, in prospect, introduce three-body effects, overcoming some limitations of the Isobar Model, and has all factors necessary to reveal the presence of CPV. To do so, it factorizes the weak vertex separated in leading topologies and relies on extensions of Resonant Chiral Perturbation Theory to describe FSI. As a proof-of-concept, a toy dataset of the S-wave of the most recent amplitude analysis of $D^+ \to K^-K^+π^+$, by the CLEO-c collaboration, was fitted with this model. From fits to model-independent parametrizations of scattering amplitudes, the parameters of the FSI amplitudes were fixed, and the production parameters of the weak vertex were then obtained from the fit to the toy dataset, yielding a good agreement between the data and our model.
papers.comments: 43rd International Conference on High Energy Physics (ICHEP 2026). Submitted to Proceedings of Science

papers.title: Next-to-leading order QCD corrections to fully charm tetraquark radiative decays
papers.summary: We present the first complete next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD calculation of the fully charm tetraquark radiative decays $T_{4c}(0^{++},2^{++})\toγJ/ψ$ and $T_{4c}(1^{+-})\toγη_c$ at leading order in the relative velocity. The NLO widths are $2.3$--$3.1$ times the leading-order (LO) widths for the long-distance matrix element (LDME) inputs considered here, with $m_c=1.5$ GeV and $μ_R=2m_c$. In the scalar channel, the NLO corrections change the relative contributions of the two color-spin components and their interference. For the tensor channel, the longitudinal fraction $f_L$ of the daughter $J/ψ$ changes from $0.11$ at LO to $0.18$ at strictly expanded NLO, with sensitivity to higher-order corrections. These NLO results provide valuable theoretical input for searches for states predicted below their respective lowest dicharmonium thresholds and for probing the spin and short-distance structure of observed tetraquark candidates.

papers.title: DAMA/LIBRA dark matter signal: a global analysis
papers.summary: The annual modulation reported by the DAMA/LIBRA collaboration remains in tension with the null results of other direct-detection experiments. We investigate the compatibility of DAMA/LIBRA with LZ, PICO-60 and CDMSlite within a generalized non-relativistic effective field theory (EFT) framework. In addition to the EFT operator expansion we investigate additional modifications to the standard WIMP picture, including inelastic scattering, variations in the NaI quenching factors, and a rescaling of the dark-matter velocity dispersion. We perform a Markov chain Monte Carlo analysis in this extended model space, using two alternative approaches to the likelihood function describing the DAMA/LIBRA data. Both approaches result in strong discrepancy between the data from DAMA/LIBRA and other experiments. We conclude that the extended model space considered here cannot accommodate the DAMA/LIBRA signal while remaining consistent with the non-observation of dark matter in other experiments.

papers.title: Multiplicity and transverse density as ordering variables of the $Λ/K^0_S$ ratio in oxygen-oxygen collisions at the LHC
papers.summary: Baryon-to-meson enhancements are commonly compared across collision systems at equal multiplicity. Using published data only, we test whether the $p_T$ dependence of the CMS $Λ/K^0_S$ ratio in minimum-bias O-O collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.36$ TeV can be obtained from CMS multiplicity-differential p-Pb and Pb-Pb measurements weighted with the O-O multiplicity distribution. The prediction from p-Pb collisions of equal multiplicity is harder than the data, with a tilt of $+0.35\pm0.04$ in $\ln(\mathrm{prediction}/\mathrm{data})$ versus $\ln p_T$, whereas that from peripheral Pb-Pb collisions is consistent with the data. In a Glauber model calibrated on O-O data, O-O and peripheral Pb-Pb collisions of equal multiplicity have similar transverse densities $ρ=\langle(dN_{ch}/dη)/S_\perp\rangle$, about half of that in p-Pb. Matching the p-Pb reference in $ρ$ instead of multiplicity reduces the tilt by about 60%, to $+0.14\pm0.04$, with nucleons as sources; the tension is fully removed ($-0.02\pm0.04$) only when sub-nucleonic structure is included (three constituents per nucleon), so the conclusion depends on the modeled size of high-multiplicity p-Pb collisions. The published blast-wave velocities of p-Pb and Pb-Pb collisions, which differ at equal multiplicity, are close at equal $ρ$. Multiplicity alone thus does not determine the $Λ/K^0_S$ shape across systems; the data are consistent with a radial boost governed by the transverse density, as expected from hydrodynamics. The same pattern is found in EPOS4, which has a hydrodynamic core, but not in PYTHIA Angantyr. For Ne-Ne collisions, which have the transverse density of O-O at equal multiplicity, the minimum-bias ratio is predicted to agree with O-O within 3-5%, as EPOS4 also predicts.

papers.title: Electroweak corrections to the SM-like Higgs boson decays and the Higgs trilinear coupling in the real Higgs triplet model
papers.summary: We study new physics effects on the decays of the standard model-like Higgs boson ($h$) and the Higgs trilinear coupling including the full one-loop corrections in the real Higgs triplet model (RHTM). We adopt the on-shell renormalization scheme, in which the scalar mixing angles are renormalized in a gauge-independent way using the pinch technique. We found that sizable one-loop effects can arise in the decay rates through the Higgs wave-function (external-leg) corrections, while the tree-level effects are rather small due to the constraint on the vacuum expectation value of the triplet field from the electroweak precision measurements. In addition, the $h\toγγ$ decay rate and the $hhh$ coupling are sensitive to loop contributions. The RHTM may be distinguishable from other extended Higgs models by studying the correlations among the $h\toττ$, $h\to ZZ^{*}$, and $h\toγγ$ decay modes, and such characteristic predictions can be tested at the High-Luminosity LHC or future Higgs factories.

papers.title: Study of enhancing the signal-background separation for the Higgs boson production in association with a single top-quark in $pp$ collisions at the LHC
papers.summary: In this paper, a multivariate analysis based approach for enhancing the extraction of the rare Standard Model (SM) process being studied - Higgs boson production in association with a single top quark (tH) - from the prevailing background processes is presented. The analysis was performed using a Monte Carlo generated dataset simulating the outcomes of proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). A deep fully connected neural network was developed for signal-background discrimination, incorporating a masking mechanism designed to suppress the contribution of input variables associated with objects that were not reconstructed in a given event. The performance of the masked architecture was evaluated on independent Monte Carlo samples. The results of the proposed methodology are compared with a conventional cut-based approach in terms of the statistical significance of the tH production channel. The developed framework was tested using a simulated dataset corresponding approximately to the combined statistical samples of LHC Runs 1, 2, and 3.

papers.title: Investigating nucleon resonances in the $pp\to K^+K^+ΛΛ$ reaction
papers.summary: In this work, we investigate the \(pp \to K^+ K^+ ΛΛ\) reaction using an effective Lagrangian approach and the isobar model. The calculation includes the exchange of \(π\), \(η\), \(σ\), \(ρ\), \(ω\), and \(K\) mesons, as well as contributions from eight nucleon resonances: \(N(1535)\), \(N(1650)\), \(N(1710)\), \(N(1720)\), \(N(1895)\), \(N(1900)\), \(N(2060)\) and \(N(2120)\). The double-resonance excitation mechanism (\(NN \to N^* N^*\)) is found to dominate this reaction over the entire energy range considered. Among the exchanged mesons, the \(η\) exchange provides the largest contribution at lower energies, whereas the \(K\) exchange dominates at higher energies. Near the threshold, \(N(1535)\) and \(N(1650)\) play the most important roles, while at higher energies \(N(1710)\) and \(N(1720)\) become dominant. Due to isospin conservation, this reaction is predominantly coupled to nucleon resonances, providing a relatively clean channel for \(N^*\) spectroscopy. Our results indicate the unique potential of this reaction for studying nucleon resonances and provide a theoretical reference for future experimental studies at HIAF.

papers.title: dSIBP: a package for generating IBP seeds for QFT in de Sitter spacetime
papers.summary: Recent studies show that in addition to the flat spacetime, Integration-by-parts (IBP) relations and differential equations can also provide a systematic approach to Feynman integrals in de Sitter spacetime. dSIBP is a Mathematica package for the automated construction of IBP systems and differential equations. For dS integral families with massive and massless propagators, it generates a complete set of IBP seeds, assembles linear systems for external reduction, and constructs differential equations for the reduced master integrals. The implementation combines equations of motion, remaining terms and parity constraints, and provides reliable checks. We describe the conventions and public interface through worked examples.

papers.title: Twist-three quark TMDs from back-to-back dijet production in next-to-eikonal DIS
papers.summary: We study back-to-back dijet production in deep inelastic scattering (DIS) at next-to-eikonal accuracy within the Color Glass Condensate framework, focusing on the quark-background contributions. We compute the quark-gluon and quark-antiquark production cross sections through next-to-leading power in the correlation limit for longitudinally and transversely polarized photons. In the quark-gluon channel, we derive both the kinematic corrections to the hard parts accompanying the twist-two quark distribution and the genuine twist-three contributions involving three-body quark-gluon-quark correlators. In the quark-antiquark channel, the interference of the eikonal amplitude with the double $t$-channel quark-exchange amplitudes probes three-body correlators with a different transverse arrangement of the fields. We express the results in terms of transverse momentum dependent (TMD) correlators and provide the corresponding hard coefficients. Our analysis extends the operator-level connection between the next-to-eikonal CGC framework and quark TMDs beyond leading power in the correlation limit.

papers.title: Light Mediators at the Neutrino-Dark Matter Frontier: Coherent Scattering, Precision Constraints, and Complementary Searches
papers.summary: Low-threshold neutrino and dark-matter experiments constrain light mediators through different momentum transfers, targets, and coupling combinations. We examine scalar and vector interactions in coherent neutrino--nucleus scattering, neutrino--electron scattering, and dark-matter direct detection. Three representative interaction models are used to compare recoil spectra and coupling degeneracies. For $^{73}\mathrm{Ge}$ and $^{131}\mathrm{Xe}$, the nuclear-charge response matrix has a condition number of approximately 115, so two different targets may still leave nearly parallel blind directions. An analytic profile-likelihood calculation shows how spectral overlap and uncertainties in neutrino interactions affect dark-matter discovery sensitivity in the neutrino fog. We discuss the implications of measurements from COHERENT, CONUS+, LZ, XENONnT, and PandaX-4T and specify which theoretical inputs, detector responses, and statistical correlations are needed to combine their constraints.   keyword : coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering; light mediators; neutrino--electron scattering; dark matter direct detection; non-standard interactions; solar neutrinos; complementarity

papers.title: Parton wave functions, density matrices and entropy in DGLAP evolution
papers.summary: Parton multiplicity entropy, proposed by Kharzeev and Levin as entanglement between the region probed in deep inelastic scattering and the proton's remainder, was compared with hadron multiplicity data. It is computed from parton densities, which do not fix the partons' quantum state. We show that a one-parton density matrix from Lipatov's wave functions determines two entropies for resolved modes with finite mean number and entropy. Its trace is the mean parton number, and normalization gives a sampled parton's entropy. A compatible thermal state, if it exists, maximizes entropy at fixed one-parton matrix. This maximum equals the actual entropy only for that thermal state and measures entanglement only for a specified subsystem of a pure state. The geometric multiplicity entropy follows if all emitted partons share one mode. An entropy computed from densities becomes such a maximum, an upper bound on the actual entropy, only for specified resolved modes. We also show that the state averaged over unrecorded emissions, assumed incoherent across scales, obeys probability-preserving Lindblad evolution on finitely many regulated modes with the resolution scale if emission and no-emission terms match. The occupations reproduce leading-order DGLAP, with virtual terms, at leading logarithmic accuracy as the cutoffs on momentum fractions are removed. The reduction holds for strongly ordered transverse momenta in light-cone gauge and dilute occupations, including those of newly resolved modes. Approximating momentum and helicity modes by independent thermal populations closes the occupation equation and gives this bound's evolution, with Bose and Pauli factors from the operator algebra. We propose testing this approximation at HERA or the LHC. The test compares the mode number inferred from normalized hadron factorial moments in a rapidity window with the window's transverse mode count.

papers.title: Vertex-resummed kinetic theory of dipole-symmetric bosons from 2PI effective action
papers.summary: The formalism of non-equilibrium dynamics for the dipole-symmetric $U(N)$ model involving $N$-component charged scalar fields is studied on the Schwinger-Keldysh contour by a systematic $1/N$ expansion of two-particle-irreducible (2PI) effective action to the next-to-leading order (NLO). The differential equations describing non-equilibrium evolution equations of two-point functions and field expectation values related to the symmetry breaking in the dynamics are derived, which encompass scatterings between modes essential in the late-time evolution and thermalization beyond the scope of the mean field. At the late-time regime of the evolution, the leading-order (LO) gradient expansion is performed to construct the vertex-resummed kinetic theory by encoding non-perturbative effects in the vertex through the resummation, which is distinct from the standard kinetic theory written by the weak-coupling expansion.

papers.title: How Fast do Black Holes Spin?
papers.summary: We present a systematic study of the spin evolution of accreting black holes. Using the BHAC code for general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations, we conduct a total of 500 high resolution simulations of magnetized accretion disks around Kerr BHs with spin parameters ranging from $χ=0$ to $χ= 0.99$. The baseline configuration follows the default Fishbone--Moncrief torus setup in BHAC. We further explore the effects of: I) introducing multiple poloidal magnetic loops, II) the initial position of the torus, III) magnetic field strength and IV) radial loop modulation. From each simulation we extract the mass flux and angular momentum flux through the horizon to compute the time-averaged spin evolution rate after the system becomes quasi-stationary. The equilibrium spin ranges from $χ_{\rm eq}\simeq0.88$ in the fiducial model to $χ_{\rm eq}\simeq0.98$ for weak-flux model. Applied to Sgr A$^*$, even an optimistic estimate for rapid spin evolution gives a timescale longer than $10^{13}$ yr, indicating an earlier growth or merger history. These trends are consistent with the picture that larger net magnetic flux threading the horizon enhances jet-torques and reduces the equilibrium spins, whereas weak net flux yields near-maximal spins. Our results provide a pathway to interpret the high spins reported for X-ray binaries and active galactic nuclei and they sharpen the astrophysical viability of near-horizon high-energy processes that rely on near-extremal black holes.

papers.title: Comment on "Long-range magnetic fields in the ground state of the Standard Model plasma"
papers.summary: We revisit the two-loop parity-odd photon polarization analyzed by Boyarsky, Ruchayskiy, and Shaposhnikov [Phys. Rev. Lett. 109, 111602 (2012)]. The original calculation neglected opposite- fermion-flow partner diagrams for the tadpole and exchange-bubble topologies alike. We quantify the impact of the properly restored exchange-bubble coefficients on the static magnetic response.

papers.title: Semiparametric Estimation of Physics Parameters and Parton Distribution Functions
papers.summary: The simultaneous determination of Parton Distribution Functions (PDFs) and fundamental physical parameters, e.g. the strong coupling constant $α_s$, the mass of the top quark $m_t$, or Wilson coefficients of an Effective Field Theory operators, is essential for the high-precision physics programme of the Large Hadron Collider. Yet, simultaneous global fits face significant methodological and computational challenges, rooted in the fundamental tension between estimating a finite-dimensional parameter and an infinite-dimensional function. In this paper, we address this problem by introducing a semiparametric estimation framework. The key advantage of our approach is that it avoids the need to refit the PDFs in the presence of either modified SM parameters or BSM contributions. Starting from standard, decoupled estimates of the PDFs and physics parameters, the method computes a bias correction a posteriori via the efficient influence function, yielding a debiased one-step estimator of the finite-dimensional parameter along with uncertainties with valid frequentist coverage. This correction rigorously accounts for the interplay between PDF and physics parameters without requiring a computationally expensive joint fit. As a proof of concept, we apply the method to two toy scenarios preparatory to a realistic global fit: the extraction of a dimension-six SMEFT Wilson coefficient from Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS) pseudo-data based on BCDMS measurements, isolating the non-singlet PDF combination $T_3$, and to the determination of the proton total valence $V$ from combined HERA measurements. Our results demonstrate that the one-step estimator successfully removes the bias inherent in a preliminary, decoupled estimate and achieves confidence intervals with correct nominal coverage, offering a statistically rigorous and computationally efficient alternative to full simultaneous PDF fits.

papers.title: Observable gravitational waves from unstable ALP catastrogenesis
papers.summary: We focus on gravitational waves (GWs) observable in pulsar timing array and interferometric searches that are produced by the annihilation of cosmic string-wall networks in axion-like particle (ALP) models. We called this process "catastrogenesis." It produces GWs with a characteristic peaked spectrum. These GWs would not be observable if the ALPs were stable. We thus assume that ALPs decay into two photons before Big-Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN). The large ALP-photon coupling required could induce field dissipation and friction on cosmic walls through interactions with the radiation background. We study the conditions under which these effects are negligible and map the parameter regions yielding observable GW signals onto the usual ALP mass-coupling parameter space. We find that, in these regions, ALPs dominate the energy density of the Universe before they decay, leading to a period of intermediate matter domination, which would leave a clear imprint on the GW spectrum.

papers.title: Revisiting the gamma-ray signal from light ALPs emitted during the evaporation of memory-burdened PBHs
papers.summary: The memory-burden effect was recently proposed to take into account the information back-reaction in the evaporation of primordial black holes (PBHs). In this work, we systematically explore the axion-like particle (ALP) production via the evaporation of memory-burdened PBHs and the subsequent ALP-photon conversion in cosmic magnetic fields. The PBH evaporation progress is divided in the semiclassical phase of Hawking radiation and the quantum memory-burden phase. The time evolution of PBH mass and the gamma-ray flux after the conversion of PBH-emitted ALP are then evaluated by considering the memory-burden induced PBH entropy suppression. Furthermore, we investigate the detection prospects of this evaporation-conversion signal in next-generation satellite telescopes, including AMEGO, e-ASTROGAM and MAST. The detectable PBH mass range is extended down to masses much smaller than $10^{15}$ g. Applying the Fisher forecasting method, we derive the projected sensitivity for PBH fraction $f_{\rm PBH}$ and ALP-photon coupling $g_{aγγ}$.

papers.title: Holographic spin alignment of vector mesons in a spinning black-hole background
papers.summary: Holographic predictions for vector-meson spin alignment are difficult to compare between charmonium and light vector mesons, as the two sectors are typically treated in different rotating backgrounds and spectral prescriptions. Consequently, it remains unclear whether a single rotating medium can generate the opposite polarization preferences observed in data. We address this by placing \(J/ψ\) and \(φ\) in one soft-wall model on the planar limit of a five-dimensional equal-spin Myers--Perry (MP) AdS black hole, computing spectral functions and spin alignment within the same current-correlator framework; the nonrotating results of Sheng et al. [Phys. Rev. D 110, 056047 (2024)] are recovered at \(a=0\). At \(T=0.15~\mathrm{GeV}\), \(J/ψ\) retains a clear resonance peak, whereas \(φ\) shows no narrow peak and instead behaves as a broad distribution consistent with unstable \(s\bar{s}\) pairs. For \(J/ψ\) along \(z\), rotation enhances the positive deviation of \(ρ_{00}^{h}\) from \(1/3\) at low and intermediate momenta but suppresses it at high momenta; along \(x\), the effect is small. For \(φ\), rotation enhances the negative deviation, more along \(z\) than along \(x\). The opposite helicity-frame signs and the opposing azimuthal and rapidity trends of the global alignment provide a reference for interpreting data: trends inconsistent with these would challenge the simplest single homogeneous rotating-medium interpretation. We distinguish model-dependent numerical details from qualitative features stable within this model class.

papers.title: Generative Modeling for Cascading Extremes via Autoregressive Transformers
papers.summary: Extreme events often occur sequentially, from earthquake-tsunami cascades to successive extreme losses in financial markets. We introduce an extremal token representation that encodes multivariate observations as a categorical sequence. A quiet token records the absence of threshold exceedances; otherwise, the token identifies the exceeding component with the largest marginal probability-scale score. The representation is invariant to componentwise strictly increasing transformations. It preserves the identity and temporal ordering of dominant exceedances but discards their magnitudes and the identities of nondominant simultaneous exceedances. A decoder-only transformer estimates the history-dependent next-token kernel on this representation, and recursive sampling generates future token sequences from the induced joint predictive law. We amortize our generative model by pretraining across simulated process families with varying parameters and dependence persistence. Next-token predictions are evaluated against exact conditional probabilities for held-out categorical processes and particle filter references for heavy-tailed vector autoregressive processes. Applied to ten-second returns for five semiconductor stocks, the pretrained model supports zero-shot transfer, while a few epochs of adaptation improve agreement between observed and generated token frequencies and transition patterns. These results support task-specific tokenization and simulation-based pretraining for modeling which dimensions dominate multivariate extremes.

papers.title: Balance-Guided Forest for Causal Effect Estimation
papers.summary: Covariate balancing is widely used for estimating causal effects in observational studies. A central challenge is determining which covariate features should be balanced. Forest-kernel balancing provides a data-driven way to learn informative balancing features. Existing forest-kernel balancing methods first learn a tree-based representation and then construct balancing weights. However, this procedure creates a mismatch, as limited tree capacity may be spent on features that are already well represented. We propose Balance-Guided Forest (BGF), which uses the current balancing weights to guide subsequent tree construction. BGF grows trees using a novel splitting score that combines residual imbalance with an outcome contrast, favoring splits that separate outcome-relevant regions where imbalance remains. This couples representation learning with covariate balancing rather than treating balancing as a downstream step. We establish an oracle-type bound that links the iterative construction to weighting error and causal bias. Simulations exhibit improvements in causal estimation relative to existing forest-kernel approaches. Real-data applications illustrate the practical behavior of BGF across observational studies.

papers.title: From Type to Token: Petri Nets, Individual Token Philosophy, and Individualized Causal Effects
papers.summary: Structural Causal Models and Bayesian Networks are the dominant framework for representing causal relations. They are fundamentally type-level formalisms since their estimands, Average Treatment Effects and Conditional Average Treatment Effects, are properties of distributions over populations, not of individual units. When treatment effects exhibit unbounded heterogeneity, these estimands collapse. What persists is the structural, token-level core of causation.   We argue that Petri Nets under the Individual Token Philosophy are the natural representation of these token-level causal structures. We develop a formal translation from Bayesian Networks to Petri Nets, providing a two-layer account of individualized causality. The PN layer provides a structural representation of causal mechanisms that does not rest on distributional assumptions. In turn, a conformal prediction layer quantifies causal effects with finite-sample coverage guarantees. Together they constitute a complete account of individual causal effects.

papers.title: Exact signal recovery from generative priors with sigmoid output activation
papers.summary: We show exact signal recovery in generative compressed sensing for feedforward neural networks with piecewise-linear activations and a final sigmoid activation, with no assumption of expansivity. Consider a ReLU network of depth $d$ with a sigmoid final activation, whose input layer, of dimension $k$, is the narrowest, and let $K$ be the geometric mean of the widths of its layers. We show that, with high probability, all signals of the range whose entries lie in $[δ, 1 - δ]$ are uniformly recovered from $m \gtrsim k(d \log(K/k) + \log(1+\log(1/δ)))$ measurements.

papers.title: Transport along Local Annealing Paths: Wasserstein Geometry and Multimodal Sampling
papers.summary: Variational approaches to learning transport maps for multimodal sampling can suffer from mode collapse. One way to mitigate this problem is to learn transport along a prescribed path of intermediate distributions defined by geometric annealing. We show that annealing can take a substantial detour in Wasserstein space: when mass moves between modes, the path can be much longer than the distance between its endpoints. We further link path geometry to transport learning, showing that long annealing paths can slow population optimization, while sufficiently regular paths permit rapid convergence. Motivated by these findings, we propose componentwise annealed transport (CAT) to reduce the need for mass transfer between modes. Starting from a mode-informed mixture reference, CAT constructs an exact mixture decomposition of the target and learns separate transport maps along componentwise annealing paths. We estimate the component weights separately and show that these estimates remain consistent even when the learned flows are inexact. We also develop adaptive annealing schedules guided by transport effort. Experiments on multimodal synthetic distributions and Bayesian inference problems demonstrate improvements in transport learning and sampling efficiency.

papers.title: Near-Minimax Sample Complexity for Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning under Generative Models
papers.summary: In multi-objective reinforcement learning, preferences may be specified only after data collection, requiring one dataset to support a continuum of reward trade-offs. We study finite discounted Markov decision processes with unknown transitions, $S$ states, $A$ actions, and $m$ known reward functions taking values in $[0,1]$, given access to a generative model. The learner must provide an $\varepsilon$-optimal policy for every convex combination of these rewards without further sampling, with a guarantee that holds simultaneously over all preferences and initial states. Writing $H=(1-γ)^{-1}$, we establish the constant-confidence minimax sample complexity $\widetildeΘ\!\left(   \frac{SAH^3}{\varepsilon^2}\min\{S,\log(em)\} \right)$, where the suppressed factors are logarithmic in $S,A,H,\varepsilon^{-1}$ and the dependence on $m$ is explicit. Thus, up to these logarithmic factors, the worst-case statistical cost of supporting all preferences grows logarithmically with the number of objectives and saturates at the number of states. The upper bound uses uniform state--action sampling and empirical planning, with reward rounding in the logarithmic-objective regime. Its analysis chains optimal-value increments over covers of the reward hull. A one-sided Bellman variance bound controls signed value differences under a second transition kernel, preserving the $H^3\varepsilon^{-2}$ dependence. A complementary uniform guarantee for all bounded rewards yields the state-dimension saturation. We establish lower bounds matching up to logarithmic factors through a rare-exit construction with subset rewards and action encoding. These bounds apply to adaptive simulator queries and arbitrary randomized history-dependent output policies, while the upper bounds are attained by deterministic stationary policies.

papers.title: Support Vector Machines Directly Minimise KL Divergence
papers.summary: Support vector machines (SVMs) are fundamentally grounded in geometric margin maximisation and currently lack a mainstream probabilistic interpretation. This keeps them theoretically isolated from probabilistic machine learning models that are naturally comparable and combinable. In this paper, we bridge this gap by proving that the dual objectives of both support vector classification and support vector regression are exact, constrained Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence minimisation tasks between two Gaussian measures. We further show that this same divergence formulation recovers the exact objective function for kernel ridge regression when domain constraints are removed and $L^2$ regularisation is applied. By demonstrating that SVM duals directly minimise relative entropy, our results provide a unified information-theoretic model for standard kernel machines and lay the foundation for unifying broader kernel-based algorithms under probability theory.

papers.title: A Unified Framework for Training-Dataset Aggregation and Exact Machine Unlearning via Gibbs Probability Measures
papers.summary: In this paper, three operations on Gibbs probability measures are studied: renormalization, normalized log-linear combination, and nesting. The resulting measures are shown to be Gibbs probability measures with explicit expressions for their objective functions, reference measures, and regularization factors. These measures are further characterized as unique solutions to optimization problems involving linear combinations of the original objective functions, subject to either relative entropy regularization or relative entropy constraints. When the reference measures are probability measures, geometric interpretations of these three operations are established involving Pythagorean identities and exponential geodesics.A central result is the equivalence between nesting and normalized log-linear combinations of Gibbs probability measures. These results are then applied to supervised machine learning with Gibbs algorithms, which are represented by Gibbs probability measures. In this context, either through nesting or log-linear combinations, Gibbs algorithms trained on local datasets are used to form new Gibbs algorithms trained upon the aggregation of all local training datasets. Interestingly, the parameters of such operations, determine the weights of each training data point on the aggregated dataset. %Operations on local Gibbs probability measures are shown to control the contributions of training data. This observation is leveraged for achieving: (a) exact machine unlearning in centralized, decentralized, and federated learning systems; and (b) centralized-equivalent performance, in the sense of producing algorithms trained on the aggregation of all local datasets in decentralized and federated learning .
papers.comments: Submitted to the IEEE Transaction on Information Theory

papers.title: Generalized Hyperrectangular Prediction Sets in Multivariate Conformal Prediction
papers.summary: In multivariate conformal prediction, many nonconformity scores yield prediction sets with complex geometry (e.g., ellipsoids or density level sets) that are difficult to interpret and visualize.
